item.content:encoded:
ABOUT THE HUB

A quieter way to find your next step

Herts Wellbeing Hub is a student guide to parks, gyms, sports, and support around the University of Hertfordshire. It is here for the days when you want to move, get outside, or find help, without searching through several different sites first.

What you can find

  • Parks and walking: green spaces and short routes near campus.
  • Gym and fitness: University gyms and a nearby leisure centre, with prices only where they are published.
  • Sports and activities: pitches, courts, and places to play.
  • Wellbeing: a clear route to the Universityâ€™s own support pages.

Who it is for

The hub is written for University of Hertfordshire students, including students who are new to Hatfield and students who travel by train or bus. You do not need to be training already. A short walk, a first gym visit, or a look at student support all count.

Places are grouped by what you want to do: parks and walking, gyms, and sports. Each park also shows how hard the route is, so a beginner and a regular runner can choose differently.

How recommendations are written

Every gym, park, and sports venue is recommended. Where a score is shown, it is moderate or higher. Prices and distances are included only when a venue has published them.

Cookie choices are at the bottom of every page: essential storage for sign-in, or optional cookies if you also want the sign-in video.

Start with one place. The rest can wait.

Discover Parks & Walking Routes in Hertfordshire

Looking for fresh air, peaceful surroundings or a way to stay active without spending much money?

Hertfordshire has plenty of green spaces and walking routes to explore. Discover places where University of Hertfordshire students can enjoy nature, walk with friends and take a break from studying.

Stanborough Park

Stanborough Park in Welwyn Garden City is a lovely place to enjoy the outdoors. With lakes, open green spaces and walking paths, it is ideal for a relaxing walk, spending time with friends or taking a break from university work. You can enjoy the natural surroundings without needing to join a gym.

Stanborough Park gives University of Hertfordshire students a chance to relax after lectures, reduce stress and improve their physical well-being.

Students can enjoy walking, watersports and picnics with friends, helping them stay active and balance university life with leisure.

Verulamium Park

Located in St Albans, Verulamium Park is a beautiful green space with a lake, open lawns and scenic walking paths. It's a great place for students to enjoy a peaceful walk, meet friends or take a break from busy university life

Take a relaxing stroll through Verulamium Park and enjoy its peaceful lake, open green spaces and beautiful surroundings. Whether you're walking alone or catching up with friends, it's a lovely way to spend time outdoors in St Albans.

Explore Local Walking Route

Walking is an easy and affordable way to stay active while exploring Hertfordshire. Whether you prefer a short stroll or a longer walk, local parks and nature trails offer opportunities to enjoy fresh air, discover new places and take a break from studying.

Hatfield to Ellenbrook Field

Ellenbrook Fields is a green open space near Hatfield, making it a useful option for students who want to spend time outdoors.

Enjoy a walk through the open landscape, get some fresh air and take a break from your university routine. Check the route and access conditions before setting off

Walking is an easy and affordable way to stay active while exploring Hertfordshire. Whether you prefer a short stroll or a longer walk, local parks and nature trails offer opportunities to enjoy fresh air, discover new places and take a break from studying.

Free & Budget-Friendly Activities

Staying active doesn't have to be expensive! Hertfordshire has outdoor spaces where students can enjoy walking, fresh air and time with friends without paying gym membership fees. Always check local travel costs, parking charges and any activity fees before visiting.

  • Enjoy a park walk : Explore local green spaces and walking paths.
  • Walk with friends : Make your daily walk more enjoyable by going with classmates.
  • Explore nature : Discover new places, take photographs and enjoy the outdoors.

Tips for a Safe and Enjoyable Walk

  • Wear comfortable shoes: Choose footwear suitable for the route.
  • Check the weather: Take a coat or umbrella if rain is expected.
  • Plan your route: Check the distance and directions before leaving.
  • Bring water: Stay hydrated, especially on longer walks.

Ready to explore Hertfordshire? Grab your comfortable shoes, invite a friend and discover the green spaces around you. Small steps can make a big difference to your daily wellbeing!

Find Gyms & Fitness in Hertfordshire

Looking to stay active while studying at the University of Hertfordshire? This guide helps you explore gyms, fitness facilities and exercise opportunities around Hertfordshire.

Whether you prefer working out independently, joining a fitness class or exercising with friends, you can compare options and find activities that suit your interests and budget.

University of Hertfordshire Sports Village

The University of Hertfordshire Sports Village in Hatfield offers students opportunities to stay active and enjoy a range of sports and fitness activities.

It is a convenient option to explore if you want to exercise, improve your fitness or take part in activities alongside your studies. Check the official facilities, opening hours and membership prices before visiting.

Make time for your fitness alongside your studies and explore the facilities available at the Sports Village and check which activities and membership options suit your needs and student budget.

Local Gyms & Fitness Centres

Hertfordshire has a range of local gyms and fitness centres for students who want to stay active. Depending on your location and budget, you can explore options offering gym equipment, fitness classes and workout spaces. Before joining, compare membership prices, student discounts, facilities and travel costs to find the best option for you.

Affordable Fitness for Students

Staying fit as a student doesn't have to be expensive. Before paying for a gym membership, look for student discounts, introductory offers and pay-as-you-go options.

You can also save money by using outdoor fitness spaces, following free workout videos or exercising with friends. Compare the available options to find something that fits your budget and routine.

Tips for Staying Active at University

  • Set realistic fitness goals that fit around your studies.
  • Try different activities to find something you enjoy.
  • Exercise with friends to help you stay motivated.
  • Check gym opening hours and student discounts before visiting.

Your fitness journey doesn't have to be complicated or expensive. Explore the options around Hertfordshire, choose activities you enjoy and make time for your wellbeing alongside your studies. Every small step counts.

Discover Sports & Activities in Hertfordshire

Looking for fun ways to stay active and meet new people while studying at the University of Hertfordshire?

Hertfordshire offers opportunities to enjoy different sports, join activities and spend time outdoors. Whether you enjoy team sports, individual activities or trying something new, this guide will help you explore options that suit your interests and student budget.

University of Hertfordshire Sports Village

The University of Hertfordshire Sports Village in Hatfield offers facilities and activities to help students stay active. Whether you enjoy working out, swimming or taking part in sports, it is a useful place to explore opportunities to exercise alongside your studies.

Check the official website for current facilities, opening hours, membership options and student prices before visiting.

Hatfield Leisure Centre

Hatfield Leisure Centre offers opportunities for people to enjoy sports, swimming and fitness activities. It can be a useful option for University of Hertfordshire students looking to stay active outside their lectures. Before visiting, check the centre's official website for available activities, opening times, admission prices and any student discounts

Outdoor Sports & Activities

Enjoy being active outdoors with friends! Hertfordshire has parks and open spaces where students can walk, jog and enjoy outdoor activities.

You could organise a friendly game, explore a new walking route or spend time outside between lectures. Outdoor activities can be an affordable way to stay active, socialise and take a break from studying.

  • Organise a friendly football match with classmates.
  • Try badminton or another sport with friends.
  • Explore local walking and jogging routes.
  • Visit a park for outdoor exercise and fresh air.

Affordable Sports for Students

ou don't need to spend lots of money to enjoy sports! University students can look for student discounts, free activities and affordable local facilities. Playing sports with friends, joining university activities or visiting outdoor spaces can help you stay active without stretching your budget. Compare prices and check whether facilities offer student memberships before signing up.

Tips for Getting Involved in Sports

  • Try different sports to discover what you enjoy.
  • Invite friends or classmates to join you.
  • Check activity schedules and prices before visiting.
  • Start at your own pace and choose activities that suit your fitness level.

Getting involved in sports is a great way to stay active, meet people and enjoy your time at university.

Explore the facilities and activities around Hertfordshire, find something you enjoy and make time for exercise alongside your studies. Every activity is a chance to learn something new.

Discover Wellbeing in Hertfordshire

University life can be exciting, but balancing lectures, assignments and personal life can sometimes feel overwhelming. Taking time to look after your wellbeing is important. Hertfordshire offers parks, leisure facilities and activities where students can relax, stay active and take a break from their studies. This guide helps you explore options that support both physical and mental wellbeing

Swimming for Physical and Mental Wellbeing

Swimming is a great way to combine physical activity with relaxation. Swimming pools and leisure centres around Hertfordshire give students opportunities to exercise, build confidence and take a break from studying.

You can swim at your own pace and choose a session that suits your schedule. Check local facilities for opening times, admission prices and student discounts before visiting.

Make time for yourself! Swimming can be an enjoyable way to stay active, unwind and create a healthy balance between university work and personal time.

Yoga and Group Fitness Classes

Yoga and group fitness classes can provide opportunities for students to stay active, manage everyday stress and connect with others. Students in Hatfield and the surrounding area can explore classes offered by local leisure centres and fitness providers. Activities and prices vary by provider, so check current timetables, booking requirements and student discounts before attending.

Yoga and group fitness classes offer structured opportunities to exercise, develop healthy routines and take time away from academic responsibilities.

University Wellbeing Support

University life can bring academic and personal challenges. University of Hertfordshire students can explore the support services available through the university, including resources for mental wellbeing and guidance on accessing further support.

Visit the university's official website to find current services, eligibility information and contact details.

Explore university support

Outdoor Activities for Wellbeing

Spending time outdoors can provide a welcome break from academic responsibilities. Activities such as walking, cycling and exploring nature trails offer opportunities to stay active, enjoy fresh air and spend time with friends. Students can explore outdoor activities around Hertfordshire and choose options that suit their interests, fitness levels and budgets. Check local routes and access information before setting off.

Explore Hertfordshire’s countryside

Affordable Wellbeing Activities

Looking after your wellbeing does not have to be expensive. Students can explore free or low-cost activities around Hertfordshire, including walking, cycling, university activities and community events.

Taking regular breaks, spending time outdoors and connecting with others can help create a healthier balance between studying and personal life. Check activity details and any associated costs before attending.

  • Explore free activities organised by the university.
  • Look for student discounts on local activities.
  • Spend time outdoors when the weather permits.
  • Make time for hobbies and social activities alongside your studies.

Wellbeing looks different for everyone. Explore the options available around Hertfordshire, choose activities that suit your needs and make time for yourself alongside your university commitments. Small, consistent steps can help you build a healthier and more balanced student lifestyle.

item.title: Walking in Hatfield
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
You do not need a car or a gym membership to stay active at Herts. Hatfield and the paths around College Lane and de Havilland have free walks for a free period, an evening wind-down or a weekend reset. Start here, then open each place page for detail.

What you can do here

  • Ellenbrook Fields — grassland and woodland beside de Havilland (watch for grazing cattle)
  • Roe Hill Park, Howe Dell Woods and Oxleys Wood — shorter walks in Hatfield
  • The Alban Way — traffic-free former railway path towards St Albans
  • Hatfield Park woodland walks — ticketed; check Hatfield House first
  • Longer days out — Stanborough Park, Sherrardspark Wood, Heartwood Forest or Panshanger Park

Getting there from campus

Ellenbrook Fields and the Alban Way are walkable from de Havilland; from College Lane use the shuttle or a short bus or bike hop. Town parks such as Roe Hill are a walk or short bus across Hatfield. For Welwyn Garden City woods and lakes, use Uno buses or the train.

Why students like it

Walking is free, flexible and easy with friends. Start with Ellenbrook Fields if you want something close; save Stanborough or Heartwood for a clear afternoon. Wear shoes that cope with mud, take water, and stick to marked paths.

item.title: Hatfield Park
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
A SENSE OF PLACE

History

Deer parks were recorded at Hatfield by the 13th century, and Hatfield House was built for Robert Cecil in the early 17th century near the site of the Old Palace. The estate preserves medieval wood-pasture, including pollarded veteran trees and grazing land shaped over centuries, and an ancient oak associated with the young Princess Elizabeth hearing of her accession. These dates describe the historic estate, not the opening of todayâ€™s visitor park. The information available does not date when its current gardens, woodland trails, or visitor facilities were added.

MAKE THE MOST OF YOUR VISIT

Facilities

  • Formal gardensSeasonal estate gardens; check Hatfield House visitor information for opening dates.
  • Woodland and meadowEstate landscape with veteran oak, hornbeam and beech trees.
  • Deer herdMenil fallow deer live in the parkland.

Walking and running routes

The estate has three nature trails through the park and woodland; the longest passes veteran trees.

Trail access is seasonal and route lengths vary. Check the estate map and opening information before setting out.

Why this park may suit you

Choose Hatfield Park if you want a seasonal estate visit with gardens, woodland scenery, deer and three nature trails. The trails suit a scenic walk; the published information does not identify a dedicated running track.

BEFORE YOU SET OFF

item.title: Ellenbrook Recreation Ground
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Ellenbrook Recreation Ground on Ellenbrook Lane, Hatfield (AL10 9RW) is a local park and play area close to the Ellenbrook / de Havilland side of town. It is a practical spot for a short outdoor break, a kickabout or outdoor gym work when you do not have time for a longer trip to Stanborough or Verulamium.

What you can do here

  • Use the fenced playground (including climbing kit and swings)
  • Play informal football or basketball on the goals and half-court
  • Try the outdoor gym equipment
  • Sit outside between lectures or after the gym at nearby Sports Village

Getting there from campus

From de Havilland campus it is a short walk or bike ride along Ellenbrook Lane. From College Lane, take a bus towards Ellenbrook / St Albans Road or cycle via local roads — typically 10–20 minutes depending on mode. Street parking nearby is limited; walking or cycling is easiest.

Why students like it

It is free, local and low-pressure: useful for a quick reset without planning a full park day. Facilities are outdoor and weather-dependent, so it works best as a short visit rather than a destination trip.

item.title: Stanborough Park
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Stanborough Park (Stanborough Lakes) on Stanborough Road, Welwyn Garden City (AL8 6DF) is a large lakeside park with two main lakes, trails, play areas and a watersports centre run by Better. At around 126 acres it is one of the best “big day out” green spaces near Hatfield.

What you can do here

  • Walk or run the lakeside paths and nature trails
  • Try watersports on the South Lake (sailing, kayaking, canoeing, paddleboarding when sessions run)
  • Hire rowing boats or pedalos on the North Lake in season
  • Use Splashlands and the play park in warmer months (seasonal)
  • Join Stanborough parkrun on Saturday mornings (free; check the event page)

Getting there from campus

Uno buses between Hatfield and Welwyn Garden City serve the Stanborough Road corridor; the park is also a short hop from Welwyn Garden City station by bus or bike. Pay-and-display parking is available and gets busy on sunny days. From College Lane allow roughly 20–35 minutes.

Why students like it

Lakes, long paths and optional watersports make it more interesting than a plain town park. Boat hire, open-water swim slots and café hours change by season — confirm on the Better Stanborough Park page before you go.

item.title: Oxleys Wood
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Oxleys Wood is a small local woodland nature reserve in south Hatfield (about 1.3 hectares), managed by Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council. It is handy when you only have 30–45 minutes and want trees and a pond without leaving town.

What you can do here

  • Follow the circular trail through oak, ash, elm, willow and poplar woodland
  • Visit the pond and wetter northern area (paths can be muddy)
  • Watch common birds and insects in a compact urban nature site
  • Pair a short walk with nearby streets and allotments on the return loop

Getting there from campus

Access is from Deerswood Avenue in south Hatfield (opposite Badgers Way). From College Lane it is a short bus ride or a longer walk/cycle across town. There is no large visitor car park — arrive on foot or by bike where possible.

Why students like it

It is free, close and low-effort: a proper pocket of nature when a big country park feels too far. Parts flood after heavy rain, so wear sturdy shoes and check conditions via the council Oxleys Wood page if the weather has been wet.

item.title: Sherrardspark Wood
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Sherrardspark Wood is an ancient oak and hornbeam woodland on the north-west edge of Welwyn Garden City. It is a Local Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest (around 80 hectares), so it is one of the best nearby places for a quiet, shady walk under mature trees.

What you can do here

  • Walk or jog on the network of footpaths and bridleways
  • Build a short family-friendly loop or a longer woodland circuit
  • Spot woodland birds and seasonal wildflowers
  • Combine a visit with Welwyn Garden City town centre afterwards

Getting there from campus

Travel to Welwyn Garden City by Uno bus or train from Hatfield, then walk into the wood from the town side or use the Rectory Road car park (often listed as free, 24-hour — confirm on the council site). From College Lane the journey is typically 25–40 minutes plus a walk into the trees.

Why students like it

It is free, peaceful and dense woodland — ideal when you want a screen break without paying for a park ticket. There is no café inside the wood, so bring water. For access notes see the Welwyn Hatfield Council Sherrardspark Wood page.

item.title: Panshanger Park
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Panshanger Park is a large country park and nature reserve between Hertford and Welwyn Garden City, with lakes, wetlands, grassland and ancient trees. Managed with Tarmac and partners including Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, it is a strong choice for a longer weekend walk away from campus.

What you can do here

  • Follow waymarked trails such as the Oak Trail, Dragonfly Trail, Repton Trail and Ancient Tree Trail
  • See the Panshanger Great Oak and other veteran trees
  • Watch wildlife around the lakes and wetlands (stay on permissive paths; do not swim)
  • Picnic or take a longer circular walk across the parkland

Getting there from campus

Main car parks are on Panshanger Lane (SG14 2TS, entry typically 8am–5pm) and Thieves Lane (SG14 2WN). Parking is pay-and-display. By public transport, trains to Hertford North leave a walk of about 1 km; some buses on Welwyn Road stop north-east of the park. From College Lane allow a longer trip — check National Rail and local bus apps for the day’s best link.

Why students like it

It feels like countryside without going far from Herts: big skies, lakes and proper trail lengths. Rules change with management notices, so read the latest visitor guidance on the Panshanger Park visit page before you go.

item.title: King George V Playing Fields
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
King George V Playing Fields on Beehive Lane, Welwyn Garden City (AL7 4BP) is a multi-sport park run with Better. It packs playgrounds, courts, pitches and outdoor fitness into one free-to-enter site — useful when you want activity options beyond a simple walk.

What you can do here

  • Use basketball courts, the skate park and multi-use games area
  • Book family tennis courts or play on the football pitches when available
  • Try the outdoor gym equipment and join health walk sessions when advertised
  • Visit the children’s playground and floodlit bowls green
  • Stop at the pavilion for a tea or coffee when it is open

Getting there from campus

Go to Welwyn Garden City by Uno bus or train from Hatfield, then continue to Beehive Lane in the south of the town (bike or local bus). Free parking is listed on site. Expect around half an hour or more from College Lane depending on connections.

item.title: Parks and Green Spaces Near Hatfield
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
When you need a break from lectures and screens, Hatfield has some excellent green spaces within easy reach of both College Lane and de Havilland campuses. Here are three reliable options that work well for walks, runs or a quiet sit outside.

Ellenbrook Fields sits on the former Hatfield Aerodrome site, next to the de Havilland campus. It is a large public nature park with grassland, woodland and wetland habitats, plus permissive paths for walking and cycling. You will often see Longhorn cattle grazing in fenced areas — keep dogs on a lead near them. Parking is available at Notcutts Garden Centre, and bus routes along Hatfield Road / St Albans Road make it reachable without a car. It is free to enter and ideal for a long stroll or an easy run.

Stanborough Park is a short hop towards Welwyn Garden City (just off the A1(M) junction 4). This 126-acre park has two lakes, nature trails and lakeside paths. It is a good choice when you want a longer outing with somewhere to sit and take in the view. Pay-and-display parking is available; trains to Welwyn Garden City and local buses also serve the area.

Hatfield Park (the parkland around Hatfield House) offers marked woodland and park walks when it is open to visitors. Entry is ticketed for the gardens, park and woodland walks, so check opening times and prices on the Hatfield House website before you go. It is a calmer, more formal option than Ellenbrook Fields.

Quick tip: start with Ellenbrook Fields if you want something free and close to campus. Save Stanborough or Hatfield Park for a weekend when you have a bit more time. Always wear sensible shoes after rain — some paths get muddy.

item.title: Campus Sports Facilities: Sports Village and the Oval Gym
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
You do not need an expensive town-centre gym membership to stay active at Herts. The university has two main on-campus options that students use every day.

Hertfordshire Sports Village is on the de Havilland campus (Hatfield Business Park, AL10 9EU). Facilities include a large gym (110+ stations), free weights, a multi-functional training rig, a 25-metre eight-lane pool, a 12-metre climbing wall, group-exercise studios, and tennis, squash and badminton courts. There are also outdoor pitches and a MUGA. The Sports Village is open to students, staff and the wider community. Student members should check current weekday access rules for the HSV gym and pool — at the time of writing, some membership types ask students to leave the HSV gym and pool by 5pm Monday to Friday.

The Oval Gym is on the College Lane campus. It is a 24-hour gym with 50+ stations, cardio and resistance machines, and a free-weights area. It is exclusively for University of Hertfordshire students and staff, which makes it handy for early-morning or late-evening sessions around your timetable. Students can also hire the MUGA at the Oval for free.

Memberships: student plans are sold through sport.herts.ac.uk and typically cover Oval-only, HSV, Duo Gym (both gyms) or All Inclusive options. Prices change with promotions, so check the student memberships page for the latest monthly and annual figures, joining fees, and what each plan includes. You will usually need proof of enrolment on your first visit, and a UK bank account for monthly Direct Debit plans.

Getting between campuses: if you train at the Sports Village from College Lane, use the university Park and Ride / shuttle where available, especially during chargeable parking hours on de Havilland.

item.title: Budget-Friendly Ways to Stay Active at Herts
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Staying active does not have to drain your student loan. Around Hatfield and St Albans there are plenty of low-cost or free options.

Walk for free. Ellenbrook Fields, Roe Hill Park, Howe Dell Woods and the Alban Way cost nothing to use. A 30–40 minute walk a few times a week is one of the simplest ways to protect your energy and mood during a busy term.

Try a local parkrun. Ellenbrook Fields parkrun used to run next to the de Havilland campus but no longer takes place. Nearby Saturday 9am options include Stanborough parkrun (Welwyn Garden City) and Oaklands College parkrun (St Albans). Register once on parkrun.org.uk, bring a printed barcode, and turn up — it is free, and you can walk, jog or run. Check the event page before you go in case of cancellations.

Use campus outdoor spaces. The Sports Village outdoor grounds and the College Lane MUGA / 3G pitch give you somewhere to kick a ball, do intervals or stretch without paying for a private pitch hire (check booking rules for the MUGA — students can often hire it free).

Join a student club or society. Herts SU sports clubs and recreational societies are usually cheaper than private gyms or town clubs, and they add a social side that helps if you are new to the area. Look on the Students’ Union site for current lists and trial sessions.

Home / hall workouts. Bodyweight sessions (squats, press-ups, planks, walking lunges) need no kit. Pair them with a short outdoor walk and you have a solid routine for exam weeks when the gym feels like too much effort.

Student tip: start small. Two free walks and one campus session a week beats an unused paid membership.

item.title: Walking Routes Around Hatfield and St Albans
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
If you like a route with a clear start and finish, these paths are popular with Herts students and easy to fit around lectures.

The Alban Way is the standout option. It is an approximately 6.5-mile traffic-free walking and cycling trail along a former railway line between Hatfield and St Albans (part of National Cycle Network Route 61). The surface is mostly flat and paved, so it suits beginners, pushchairs and bikes. You can join it at points such as Ellenbrook Lane in Hatfield or Highfield Park in Fleetville, St Albans. Walking the full length takes roughly two hours one way; many students do a shorter out-and-back from the Hatfield end. Watch for wildlife in the verges, and look out for remnants of the old railway platforms in the undergrowth.

Ellenbrook Fields loops. From the de Havilland side you can build your own circular walk on the permissive paths through grassland and woodland. Distances are flexible — 20 minutes or well over an hour — and there are information boards about the site’s aerodrome history.

Stanborough Park lakeside paths. At Stanborough Park (Welwyn Garden City) you can combine shorter lake circuits (around 1–2.5 km options are signed) into a longer outing. Good when you want water views without travelling into London.

Practical notes: wear layers — Hertfordshire weather changes quickly. Take water, and on the Alban Way consider a bike light or reflective kit if you might finish near dusk. For public transport back from St Albans, check Intalink or National Rail rather than assuming a late bus.

Suggested first outing: Alban Way from the Hatfield end for 30–40 minutes out, then turn back. Easy, free, and a proper break from campus.

item.title: Woodland Walks Near Hatfield: Heartwood Forest and Sherrardspark Wood
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
When you want trees, quiet paths and a proper break from campus, two of Hertfordshire’s best woodlands are within easy reach of Hatfield. Both are free to enter and work well for a weekend walk with friends.

Heartwood Forest

Heartwood Forest, near Sandridge north of St Albans, is managed by the Woodland Trust. At around 347 hectares it is one of England’s largest new native forests, with young woodland, ancient woods, meadows and wide views. Three waymarked trails start from the main car park: the Magical Meander (about 2.4 km), the Wildlife Wander (about 4 km) and the Heartwood Hike (about 4.3 km). Paths can get muddy after rain, so boots help. There are no toilets on site — the nearest public ones are in Sandridge — so plan ahead and bring water.

Sherrardspark Wood

Sherrardspark Wood sits on the north-west edge of Welwyn Garden City. It is an ancient oak and hornbeam woodland, a Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest. A network of footpaths and bridleways lets you build a short loop or a longer wander. You can reach it by train to Welwyn Garden City and walking in, or use the small car park off Rectory Road. There are no cafés inside the wood, which keeps it peaceful.

How to make a day of it

Start with Heartwood if you want signed trails and open views. Choose Sherrardspark if you prefer denser woodland closer to a train station. Stick to marked paths, take litter home, and check the Woodland Trust or Welwyn Hatfield Council pages before you go if the weather has been wet.

item.title: A Day at Verulamium Park in St Albans
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Verulamium Park is one of the easiest big green spaces to reach from Hatfield, and it rewards a half-day visit. Named after the Roman city of Verulamium, the park covers about 100 acres of parkland beside the River Ver, with Roman walls still visible and St Albans Cathedral nearby.

What you will find

The main feature is the ornamental lake, popular for a gentle circular walk of roughly 1.2 km around both lakes. There is an outdoor gym area, beach volleyball courts, a children’s play space and a café overlooking the park. Verulamium Museum sits at the edge of the park if you fancy a short cultural stop after your walk. Low-lying paths can flood after heavy rain, so check St Albans City and District Council updates if the weather has been wet.

Getting there from Hatfield

You can take a train or bus into St Albans and walk into the park, or drive and use pay parking at St Michael’s or Westminster Lodge. The Alban Way traffic-free path also links Hatfield with St Albans if you prefer to walk or cycle part of the way.

A simple student outing

Meet friends for a lakeside loop, pause on a bench with a packed lunch, then head into the city centre or catch a train home. It is free to walk the park itself. Opening times and any ticketed museum entry change, so check the Enjoy St Albans or council websites before you go.

item.title: Exploring Panshanger Park: Trails, Lakes and Ancient Trees
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Panshanger Park, between Hertford and Welwyn Garden City, is a large restored landscape of woodland, lakes and riverside paths. It is privately owned with permissive public access, so stay on the signed routes and follow the site rules.

Waymarked trails

Four waymarked walks make planning easy. The Oak Trail is about 2 km from the Panshanger Lane car park and leads to the famous Panshanger Great Oak. The Dragonfly Trail is about 3 km from Thieves Lane and loops around the lakes and River Mimram. The Repton Trail is about 4 km and follows the historic landscape views. The Ancient Tree Trail is about 6.5 km for a longer outing. Surfaces vary; expect mud in wet weather.

Practical tips

Car parks are at Panshanger Lane (SG14 2TS) and Thieves Lane (SG14 2WN). Parking charges apply — check the Panshanger Park website for current rates and opening times. Dogs are welcome but must be on leads around livestock and kept out of the lakes. Do not swim in the lakes or river. There are no litter bins, so take rubbish home.

Why students like it

It is ideal when you want more space than a town park: lakes for birdwatching, quiet woodland and room to walk and talk. You can also run on the permissive paths. Check panshangerpark.tarmac.com before you travel, as paths can close without notice.

item.title: Comparing Hatfield Gyms for Students
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Hatfield has several gym options, so it helps to match the venue to your timetable, budget and how far you want to travel from College Lane or de Havilland.

On campus first

The Oval Gym on College Lane is exclusively for University of Hertfordshire students and staff, with 24-hour access and 50+ stations. Hertfordshire Sports Village on the de Havilland campus has a larger gym (110+ stations), pool, climbing wall and studios. Student memberships are sold through sport.herts.ac.uk — plans typically cover Oval-only, HSV, Duo Gym or All Inclusive. Prices and weekday access rules change, so check the student memberships page and take proof of enrolment on your first visit.

Town options

PureGym Hatfield and NRG Gym Hatfield are 24-hour commercial gyms in town, useful if you live off campus or want a simple pay-monthly deal. Hatfield Leisure Centre (Better) has a gym, studios, sports hall and squash courts. Hatfield Swim Centre combines pool access with a gym if swimming is part of your routine. David Lloyd Hatfield and The Gym Group in Welwyn Garden City are further options if you have transport.

How to choose

Start with a campus tour or a day pass where offered. Ask about student rates, induction requirements and whether classes or a pool are included. Avoid signing a long contract until you have tried one or two sessions that fit your week. Always confirm current prices and opening hours on the venue’s own website.

item.title: Your First Week at the Gym: A Beginner's Guide
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Starting at the gym can feel intimidating, especially in the first week of term. A simple plan beats guessing what to do when you walk through the door.

Before you go

Book or complete an induction if your gym offers one — the Oval Gym and Hertfordshire Sports Village both expect new members to learn the basics safely. Wear trainers you can move in, take a water bottle and a small towel, and arrive with your student ID or membership details ready. If you are unsure about form, ask a member of staff rather than copying someone on the floor.

A gentle first-week structure

Aim for two or three short visits of 30–40 minutes. Warm up with five minutes of easy cardio, then pick a mix of machine or free-weight moves that cover legs, push, pull and core — for example squats or leg press, a chest or shoulder press, a row, and a plank. Finish with a short cool-down walk and stretches. Leave ego at the door: light weights with good form build confidence faster than heavy sets you cannot control.

Make it stick

Put sessions in your calendar like lectures. Go with a flatmate if that helps you turn up. Track what you did in the notes app on your phone so week two feels familiar. If anything hurts sharply, stop and seek advice. Check your gym’s website for class timetables if you prefer a guided session after the first few solo visits.

item.title: Group Fitness Classes at Herts
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
If you struggle to stay motivated alone, group fitness classes give you a set time, a coach and a room full of people working at their own level. Hertfordshire Sports Village on the de Havilland campus runs a large class programme in two studios, and many student memberships include group exercise — confirm what your plan covers on sport.herts.ac.uk.

What to expect

Classes typically include strength, cardio, cycling and mind-body formats led by fitness professionals. Timetables change each term, so check the Sports Village site or app before you go. Arrive a few minutes early, introduce yourself to the instructor if you are new, and tell them about any injuries. You do not need to keep up with the fittest person in the room — modify moves and focus on finishing the session.

Other places to try

Hatfield Leisure Centre and Hatfield Swim Centre (both Better) also run studio classes such as Pilates, yoga and body conditioning. Commercial gyms in Hatfield may include classes in some memberships. Always check whether a class needs pre-booking and whether student rates apply.

A good starter approach

Book two different class types in your first fortnight so you can compare. Pair one class with one quiet gym or outdoor session. If a format feels wrong, switch — consistency matters more than finding the “perfect” class on day one.

item.title: No-Kit Workouts for Halls and Shared Houses
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Some weeks the gym is too far, too busy or simply not happening. A short bodyweight session in your room or kitchen still counts — and it needs no equipment.

A 20-minute room circuit

Do three rounds of: 10–15 squats, 8–12 press-ups (on your knees or against a wall if needed), 10 walking lunges per side, 20–30 second plank, and 30 seconds of marching or high knees. Rest for a minute between rounds. Keep the door clear so you have space, and use a towel or mat if the floor is hard. Open a window if you can — stuffy rooms make everything feel harder.

Pair it with outdoor movement

After the circuit, walk for 15–20 minutes around College Lane, Ellenbrook Fields, Roe Hill Park or Howe Dell Woods. Fresh air resets your head after a day of screens. If it is dark, stick to lit paths and go with a friend when you can.

Keep expectations realistic

Two or three of these sessions a week during exam season is a win. You do not need a perfect routine — you need something you will actually do. Save gym goals for quieter weeks, and use halls workouts to protect sleep, mood and energy when coursework peaks.

item.title: Joining Herts SU Sports Clubs
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Joining a university sports club is one of the fastest ways to stay active and meet people outside your course. At Herts, Club Sport sits under HertSquad and covers teams that train on campus and compete against other universities.

How joining usually works

Clubs are open to a range of abilities, not only experienced athletes. Look for free taster sessions at the start of term, then buy the relevant Club Sport membership through the booking system on sport.herts.ac.uk. Options typically include Represent (competitive university sport), Compete (recreational fixtures in sports such as badminton, basketball, table tennis and volleyball) and Performance for selected elite teams. Benefits and fees vary by sport, so read the current page before you pay.

What you get

Most Represent memberships include weekly coached training, use of campus facilities, competition entry and support for fixtures. Recreational Compete options are lighter and cheaper if you want regular play without a full league commitment. There is also a HertSquad Pass for discounted pay-as-you-play bookings.

Before you commit

Try a taster, check training times against your timetable, and ask the club about kit costs and travel to away fixtures. Societies listed on hertssu.com are a separate route if you prefer non-competitive activity. Always confirm dates, prices and eligibility on the official Herts Sport or Students’ Union sites.

item.title: Swimming in Hatfield: Sports Village and Hatfield Swim Centre
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Swimming is a low-impact way to stay fit between lectures, and Hatfield has two main indoor options students use regularly.

Hertfordshire Sports Village pool

The Sports Village on the de Havilland campus has a 25-metre, eight-lane deck-level pool. Student swim-only and wider memberships are available through sport.herts.ac.uk. Some gym memberships that include swim ask students to leave the HSV pool by late afternoon on weekdays — check the current access rules for your plan. Adult lessons are offered at extra cost. Book lanes or check the timetable before you travel across from College Lane.

Hatfield Swim Centre

Hatfield Swim Centre on Lemsford Road (run by Better) has a 33-metre main pool plus teaching and splash pools. It suits public lane swimming and lessons, and also has a gym and fitness classes on site. Opening times, session types and prices change, so use the Better website for the latest timetable and any student or concession rates.

Making it work as a student

Pack goggles and a padlock for lockers, and aim for off-peak slots if you can. If you are new to lane swimming, start in a slower lane and follow the pool etiquette signs. Never invent a training plan that ignores how you feel — short, regular swims beat rare marathon sessions.

item.title: Five-a-Side and Campus Pitches at Herts
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
If football is your reset button, you do not always need a full eleven-a-side match. Campus pitches and the College Lane MUGA make it easy to organise a kickabout around lectures.

What is on campus

Hertfordshire Sports Village has outdoor grounds and new-generation astro pitches on the de Havilland campus. On College Lane, students can often hire the MUGA at the Oval for free — confirm the current booking rules at reception or on sport.herts.ac.uk. The Sports Village also supports Club Sport football and futsal pathways if you want structured training rather than casual games.

Organising a casual game

Message your flat or course group midweek, agree a 45–60 minute slot, and book the pitch or MUGA early in busy term weeks. Bring a pump, bibs if you have them, and water. Keep teams small for five-a-side so everyone touches the ball. Respect other users, clear rubbish, and leave on time if someone has the next booking.

Beyond campus

Hatfield Leisure Centre has 3G pitch hire for larger groups when campus slots are full. Prices and availability change, so check Better’s booking pages. Whether you play casually or join a club, the goal is the same: regular movement, fresh air and a reason to look up from your laptop.

item.title: Climbing and Racquet Sports at the Sports Village
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Beyond the gym floor, Hertfordshire Sports Village offers climbing and racquet sports that suit beginners and more experienced players alike. These are useful when you want a skill-based session instead of another machine circuit.

Climbing wall

The Sports Village has an impressive 12-metre wall with overhang, vertical and slab surfaces. Competent climbers can access the wall under the right membership; beginners should book an induction or taster. All Inclusive student memberships typically include climbing access and a taster session allowance — confirm details on sport.herts.ac.uk and the Sports Village climbing page. Never climb without the required competency check or staff guidance.

Tennis, squash and badminton

Match-quality courts are available for tennis, squash and badminton, including a dedicated badminton hall. All Inclusive members often get free off-peak court time when booked online; other users can hire courts. Equipment hire may be available if you do not own a racket. Check peak and off-peak definitions before you book.

How to start

Book a beginner session for climbing, or reserve a badminton court with a friend for a light first game. Wear clean non-marking trainers for indoor courts. If you enjoy it, look at Club Sport badminton or other racquet options for regular play. Always verify current prices, inductions and booking rules on the official site.

item.title: parkrun Options Near Hatfield
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
parkrun is a free, timed 5k every Saturday morning. You can walk, jog or run, and a volunteer tail walker means nobody finishes last. It is one of the simplest ways for Herts students to build a weekend routine.

Important update

Ellenbrook Fields parkrun, which used to run next to the de Havilland campus, no longer takes place. Do not travel there expecting an event.

Nearby Saturday options

  • Stanborough parkrun — Stanborough Park, Welwyn Garden City (around AL8 6DF), Saturdays at 9:00. Multi-lap course on grass and trails near the lake; can be muddy when wet.
  • Oaklands College parkrun — Oaklands College St Albans Campus, Hatfield Road, AL4 0JA, Saturdays at 9:00. Mixed surfaces through the college grounds. Check the event page for any cancellations.
  • St Albans parkrun — Verulamium Park, Saturdays at 9:00. A popular parkland course close to the city centre.
  • Panshanger parkrun — Panshanger Park, Hertford, Saturdays at 9:00, starting near the Panshanger Lane entrance.

How to take part

Register once for free at parkrun.org.uk, print or save your barcode, and bring it every time. Check the event’s own parkrun page the night before in case of cancellation. Arrive a little early for the briefing, and volunteer when you can — the events only run because of volunteers.

item.title: Managing Exam Stress with Movement
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Exam season shrinks everything to revision timetables and late nights. Short bursts of movement will not finish your coursework for you, but they can calm your nervous system and improve focus when you sit back down.

Keep sessions short on purpose

Aim for 20–30 minutes rather than a heroic two-hour workout you will cancel. A brisk walk around Ellenbrook Fields, Roe Hill Park or the College Lane loop, a no-kit circuit in your room, or an easy swim all count. Put the session in your calendar between two revision blocks so it feels like part of the plan, not a distraction.

Use movement to interrupt spirals

When anxiety rises, change your environment: leave the library, walk for ten minutes without your phone podcast, then return with one clear next task. Pair this with basics you can control — water, a proper meal, and a fixed lights-out time most nights.

Know when to get extra help

If stress tips into feeling unable to cope, contact University of Hertfordshire Student Wellbeing via Ask Herts or email studentwellbeing@herts.ac.uk. For urgent support, use the university’s published 24/7 helpline details on the Ask Herts wellbeing pages. Movement helps many students, but it is not a substitute for professional support when you need it.

item.title: University Wellbeing Support Services at Herts
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Looking after your mental health is as important as looking after your timetable. The University of Hertfordshire provides dedicated Student Wellbeing services for enrolled students, and you do not need to wait for a crisis to use them.

What is available

Student Wellbeing can offer counselling, mental health advice, peer support and wellbeing activities, alongside accessibility and disability services. The team is based in the Hutton Hub on College Lane. You can find directions and contact details on Ask Herts — search for “Student Wellbeing” or “counselling and mental health support”.

How to get in touch

Request support through the Dean of Students enquiry routes on Ask Herts, selecting the counselling and mental health option where prompted. You can also email studentwellbeing@herts.ac.uk or call the published Student Wellbeing number on Ask Herts. For immediate wellbeing support, follow the university’s guidance on the Ask Herts “immediate wellbeing support” page, including the 24/7 helpline number listed there.

Alongside professional support

Friends, faith communities, sports clubs and simple outdoor time all help many students feel steadier day to day. Use the parks, gyms and walking guides on this site as everyday tools, and treat Student Wellbeing as the place to go when you need structured help. Always rely on Ask Herts for the latest phone numbers, opening hours and referral steps.

item.title: Sleep and Routine Tips for Students
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Sleep is the foundation of wellbeing, yet it is often the first thing to slip in halls. A few steady habits make lectures, training and mood easier to manage.

Protect a wind-down window

Pick a target lights-out time for most nights and protect the 30–45 minutes before it. Dim the main light, leave your phone charging across the room, and avoid starting a new episode or a long scroll. If your mind is busy, jot tomorrow’s top three tasks on paper so your brain does not rehearse them in bed.

Use daylight and movement

Morning light helps set your body clock. A short walk to campus, a loop of Milwards Park or a few minutes outside between lectures is enough. Regular activity — even gentle — improves sleep quality for many people, but finish hard workouts well before bedtime if they leave you wired.

Keep the basics boring

Caffeine late in the day, heavy late meals and irregular weekend sleep all disrupt the week that follows. Aim for a similar wake time even on Sundays when you can. If sleep problems persist for weeks, speak to a GP or contact Student Wellbeing via Ask Herts. Good sleep is a skill you practise, not a luxury you earn after deadlines.

item.title: Making Friends Through Activity
item.dc:creator: minahililyas787
item.content:encoded:
Friendship at university rarely appears fully formed in a lecture theatre. Shared activity gives you repeated, low-pressure reasons to see the same people — which is how most student friendships actually start.

Choose repeating commitments

A weekly Club Sport training session, a Saturday parkrun, a regular badminton booking or a walking group beats one-off events. You do not need to be talented; you need to turn up. HertSquad clubs, SU societies on hertssu.com and casual campus pitch games are all useful starting points.

Start smaller than you think

Invite one flatmate to Stanborough parkrun, ask a seminar partner to walk the Alban Way, or join a beginner climbing induction at the Sports Village. Suggest a concrete time and place rather than “we should hang out sometime”. After the session, a simple “same again next week?” keeps the door open.

Balance social time and rest

You do not have to say yes to everything. Protect sleep and study blocks, and pick one or two activities that fit your values and energy. If loneliness feels heavy or persistent, Student Wellbeing on Ask Herts can help. Activity is a powerful way to meet people — and looking after yourself is part of being a good friend too.
